title: CI auto-retry eligibility is opt-in via the auto-rerun label, not author or auto-merge
answers: Why isn't my PR being automatically rerun after a failed CI run?
How do I opt a PR into automatic CI retries without enabling auto-merge?
Which PRs does the retry workflow pick up?
body:
Symptom: a PR that failed CI is never retried automatically, even though it is open, non-draft and recent.
Root cause: .github/workflows/retry.yml, the gh api graphql search in the candidate step, selects PRs by the search string `label:auto-rerun` (plus `is:open draft:false created:>=$cutoff`), not by `author:app/dependabot` or an autoMergeRequest.
Fix pattern: to make a PR eligible, add the `auto-rerun` label. Do not reintroduce author or auto-merge filters in the search or the jq `select`.
Constraints: Only the mergeable != CONFLICTING jq filter, the three-day cutoff, pagination, retry limits and dry-run still apply. The label must exist in the repository before anything applies it.
Applies: Eligibility for the automatic CI retry sweep in this repository.
applies: Candidate selection for the automatic CI retry sweep only; not the retry.sh rerun logic itself.
says: Why was my pull request not automatically retried after a continuous integration failure?
Failed checks are not rerunning automatically on recently updated pull requests.
How do we opt a pull request into automatic retries without enabling auto merge?
Add the auto rerun label so that failed build tests trigger an automatic retry.
Automated test reruns should trigger based on labels rather than pull request author.
search: Candidate selection for the automatic CI retry sweep in .github/workflows/retry.yml relies on the label:auto-rerun search string along with is:open draft:false created:>=$cutoff, rather than filtering by author:app/dependabot or autoMergeRequest. To make an open, non-draft PR eligible for automatic rerun, the auto-rerun label must be added. Constraints including the mergeable != CONFLICTING jq filter, three-day cutoff, pagination, retry limits, and dry-run apply, without reintroducing author or auto-merge checks.
